messages:
maria: paging — alert flood for customer Xenon on Dedicated cluster us-west-2. multiple 5xx spikes + request timeouts since ~11:04 UTC. dashboard shows p95 errors jumping from ~0.5% -> 18%. tagging on-call. :rotating_light:
incident-bot: ALERT: dedicated-cluster-usw2-xenon elevated_5xx_rate (rule: 5xx > 5% over 5m) — triggered at 2001500000 — severity: page
kevin: on it. looking at gateway logs now. are we routing them to a single GPU pool?
maria: yes, their tenant is isolated to pool-23 (pinned) — traffic hasn't been re-routed automatically because pool capacity is reserved.
kevin: seeing repeated `503 upstream read timeout` in gateway. also a lot of `OOM` logs in the inference workers around the same timeframe. suspect worker eviction/GC thrash.
on-call-jen: i'm taking the page. assigning SRE-L2 to assist. jen>sre-l2: please pull `kubectl -n inference get pods` and top CPU/mem for pool-23
sre-l2: paste from node: 
```
$ kubectl -n inference get pods -o wide --selector=pool=pool-23
inference-0   Running   1/1   8d   10.0.23.45   node-09
inference-1   CrashLoopBackOff   0/1   5m   10.0.23.46   node-07
inference-2   Running   1/1   3d   10.0.23.47   node-11
```
sre-l2: top shows inference-1 memory pinned at 98% right before crash. kernel OOM kill traces in node logs.
kevin: that aligns with model KV cache growth for long prompt sessions — Xenon recently started a new batch job with long seq lengths. could be a hot-tenant causing OOMs across the pool.
maria: customer-success-alex, any planned batch jobs or rollout from Xenon?
customer-success-alex: Xenon did announce a heavy evaluation workload this morning to validate a new prompt template. they said it would be short (~2h) but maybe heavier than quoted. I just DMed their SRE to pause.
on-call-jen: immediate mitigations — 1) drain inference-1 and restart, 2) temporarily increase max_replicas for pool-23 to add headroom, 3) put a soft rate limit for Xenon via tenant throttling. we'll coordinate which order.
kevin: agree. priority order: pause customer batch -> scale pool -> restart crashloop node -> enable per-tenant throttling. scaling can take 2-4m depending on GPU provisioning.
sre-l2: scaling triggered via autoscaler config: `PATCH /autoscaler/pools/pool-23 {"max_replicas": 10}`. issuing now.
incident-bot: ACTION: autoscaler update initiated by sre-l2 at 2001500060 — target max_replicas=10
kevin: i'm also forcing a soft throttle on Xenon with this command: `redwoodctl quota set --tenant xenon --rps 200` — reduces bursty evaluation traffic.
maria: Xenon responded to Alex DM — they paused the job at 11:12 UTC.
customer-success-alex: confirmed pause from Xenon. they were surprised by errors, appreciate the proactive pause.
kevin: restarted inference-1 pod, watching for OOM. also enabled eviction backoff to avoid immediate re-scheduling onto same node until pressure clears.
sre-l2: restarted container succeeded, memory usage after restart is back to baseline. no further OOMs on node-07 in the last 2m.
on-call-jen: rolling window of 5m error rate dropping?
maria: p95 errors down to 4.2% and trending. p50 latency also improving from 850ms -> 420ms.
kevin: routing: we should avoid automatic fallback to hosted variants until team confirms quality acceptance. switching routing would reduce load but might change customer behavior. suggest keeping them on dedicated while we stabilize.
on-call-jen: noted. continue to monitor 15m. also we need to coordinate support comms. Alex, can you draft a brief update for Xenon and CSM? include impact, actions, and ask to confirm when evaluation resumes.
customer-success-alex: drafting now: "We observed elevated 5xx errors and latency during your evaluation job this morning. We paused your job at your request, restarted affected workers and increased capacity; error rates have dropped and we're monitoring. Please let us know when you want to resume. — Alex (CSM)"
maria: logging mitigation steps for postmortem: root cause: unplanned long-sequence eval causing KV cache memory growth -> OOM on one worker -> cascading request timeouts while autoscaler spun up new replicas; contributing factor: pinned reserved capacity prevented immediate fallback routing.
kevin: add: missing tenant-specific throttles for long-tail workloads should be part of Harden plan. also need an autoscaler faster-failover mode for crashloop scenarios.
sre-l2: note: we increased max_replicas as a short-term fix; need to verify cost impact on billing and whether reserved capacity contracts allow burst. billing flag shows `reserved: true` for pool-23; spike will be absorbed by Dedicated reserved pool but we should notify finance/pm.
on-call-jen: handoff — i'm going offline for 30m, on-call-jen handing to kevin for watch. kevin, you are primary until 2001501800. ping me if escalation. :white_check_mark:
kevin: taking watch. monitoring logs and gateway traces. set slack alert for p95>6%.
incident-bot: NOTE: handoff recorded — previous oncall on-call-jen -> new oncall kevin at 2001500120
kevin: 11:28 UTC — p95 error down to 1.1%, timeouts minimal. routing stable.
maria: good stabilization. recommend follow-ups: 1) temp: add per-tenant seq length guardrails and throttles 2) medium: autoscaler acceleration for crashloop detection 3) long: re-evaluate reserved pool routing policy to allow emergency spillover to compatible pool variants.
customer-success-alex: Xenon asked if we can provide a playbook to avoid future surprises for evaluation runs. I'll coordinate with solutions engineering.
sre-l2: I'll open an incident ticket and assign owners for each follow-up (auto-scale, throttle, routing policy).
on-call-jen: marking this thread resolved for now. final status: mitigated, customer paused job, pool scaled, crashloop fixed. will convert to postmortem template.
maria: thanks team. adding retention note and linking logs to incident ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2003
kevin: closing watch, will remain available if alerts re-fire. :thumbsup:
